lessons.title: Statutory rights and company documents
objectives: Separate legal minimums from unverified AITS arrangements.
explanation: Thai statutory employment protections and an employer’s additional benefits are different sources of entitlement. A company handbook may explain administration and provide more generous arrangements, but this training has not verified AITS benefits, payroll rules or leave approval channels. Ask for current employment terms, work rules, pay records and the applicable HR contact.

Keep copies of documents you are entitled to hold and ask for clarification when terms are unclear. Record the actual dates and facts of a concern. Do not assume that signing a document makes every term lawful. Individual questions require review of current Thai law, the employment relationship and relevant exceptions by a qualified HR or legal reviewer.
lessons.example: A colleague says AITS grants a particular bonus. No approved policy is supplied. Treat that as unverified, not as an entitlement.
lessons.exercise: Create two columns: statutory topics to verify and company arrangements to obtain.
lessons.model_response: Statutory: hours, rest, leave and wage protections. Company: work schedule, extra benefits, request channel and designated contacts.
key_points: Law and company benefits have different sources

lessons.title: Hours rest and holidays
objectives: Recognize the ordinary statutory baseline and its limits.
explanation: For ordinary work, Ministry of Labour guidance describes normal limits of eight hours a day and 48 hours a week, with lawful arrangements and sector exceptions requiring review. Specified hazardous work has a seven-hour daily and 42-hour weekly limit. The ordinary rest rule provides at least one hour after no more than five consecutive working hours; agreed split breaks and statutory exceptions must be checked.

The general baseline includes at least one weekly holiday with no more than six days between, at least 13 traditional holidays including National Labour Day, and at least six working days of annual holiday after one continuous year. These are legal baselines, not a statement of the AITS roster. Overtime consent, exceptions and pay should be checked separately; do not infer that a customer deadline overrides them.
lessons.example: A fictional roster appears to schedule continuous work without a break. Identify the concern and ask HR to check the actual arrangement and exceptions.
lessons.exercise: Annotate a sample 09:00–18:00 schedule with a one-hour midday break, then list what remains unknown.
lessons.model_response: Eight working hours are shown. Weekly total, holiday arrangements, actual duties and any overtime remain to be verified.

lessons.title: Leave categories and recent changes
objectives: Locate current leave guidance and avoid outdated figures.
explanation: Leave categories include sickness, necessary personal business, maternity, qualifying spouse support, sterilization, military service and training, each with conditions and payment rules. Sick leave and paid sick-leave limits are different concepts. Do not use an old overview as the sole source for current allowances.

The official explanation of the 2025 amendment, effective 7 December 2025, describes maternity leave of up to 120 days with employer-paid wages up to 60 days. It also describes up to 15 days of qualifying continuous child-care leave at 50% wages with the required medical evidence, and up to 15 days to assist a spouse who gives birth, paid in full, subject to the application and 90-day timing rules. These are statutory summaries, not AITS benefits. HR/legal review must confirm current text and individual eligibility before release.
lessons.example: An older Ministry overview still says 90 maternity days. The newer official amendment explanation supersedes that figure for the relevant covered situation.
lessons.exercise: Write a respectful request for current leave guidance without sharing medical details in a group chat.
lessons.model_response: Please confirm the applicable leave category, current entitlement, required documents and private submission channel for my circumstances.
key_points: Leave duration and pay are separate

lessons.title: Conduct confidentiality and concerns
objectives: Communicate professionally and protect personal information.
explanation: General professional practice includes accurate records, respectful communication, honesty about mistakes and protection of information entrusted to you. Collect only information needed for the legitimate task and share it only with authorized recipients through approved systems. This is privacy awareness, not a complete interpretation of Thailand’s PDPA or an AITS retention policy.

Before sending a document, check recipient, attachment, purpose and sensitivity. Never put customer passwords into a ticket or AI practice chat. For a concern, separate what you observed from what you suspect, preserve relevant evidence lawfully, and use a verified responsible channel. If the usual contact is implicated, seek an alternative authorized route. This lesson does not invent a company grievance procedure or promise a particular investigation outcome.
lessons.example: A fictional employee receives a customer list by mistake. Stop further sharing and report the misdelivery through the verified internal route.
lessons.exercise: Rewrite an accusatory message as an observation, impact and request.
lessons.model_response: The file was sent to an unintended recipient at 10:15. It contains contact details. Please advise the authorized containment and reporting steps.
lessons.thai_summary: สื่อสารอย่างสุภาพ บันทึกข้อเท็จจริง และจำกัดการเปิดเผยข้อมูล ตรวจสอบผู้รับและช่องทางก่อนส่งข้อมูลสำคัญ
